title: Semilinear counit composition is ordinary completed-ring composition
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime ell distinct from its characteristic, a finite extension E/Q_ell, and separated finite-type D.k-morphisms X -> Y -> Z of separated finite-type D.k-schemes [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Supply the published system operations and a normalized Realizations package [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Let t be a compatible compactification triangle with the quasi-compact open and intermediate-open hypotheses. Let K be an integral constructible object and impose bridgeDomain with common finite cohomological and Tor windows [def-sf-integral-compactification-comparison-data]. Then the actual semilinearComparison, the five-factor reduction/total-limit counit expression using the direct compactification identifications, equals ordinaryComparison_K formed from the ringed models, open comparisons and proper/open package of the same Realizations [def-sf-integral-ordinary-compactification-composition]. Neither constant-word q nor constantComparison nor completedComparison occurs in this conclusion.

source.place: Step 5; agent-formulated comparison obligation implementing the indicated portion of the integral compactification bridge proof, with Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941 and more-etale.tex Tags 0F7B--0F7D.

proof.text: For one compactification expand the direct identification into the open reduction mate, inverse reconstruction unit, and proper/limit comparison. The adjunct of its inverse is the reduction of that inverse followed by the actual counit. Unit naturality and the right triangle recover the inverse after total limit. Apply this to f and to g at F_f K. The intermediate counit is exactly the middle factor in semilinearComparison. The bridge domain supplies invertibility of these direct identifications.

Use the expression-realization composition equation of completedShriekIntegralComposition. Open normalization and the support-recursion equation identify its recursive comparisons with the single-letter calculation of the preceding step, while the compositors and proper/open map are the specified adjunction mates. The semilinear and ringed proper/open maps have equal inverse-open transposes, by normalization of the pullback square and adjunction conjugation; paste with the push and open compositors including their equality transports. This is the ordinary completedShriekIntegralA, before any finite evaluation.

Insert the two single-word inverse identifications and the composite direct identification. Apply total limit and cancel adjacent reconstruction units by the adjunction triangles. The remaining factors are completedShriekIntegralA conjugated by the three published compact-support realizations, precisely ordinaryComparison. Identity cases are the same triangles; empty opens and zero inputs give the unique zero morphism.

lean.statement:
theorem semilinearOrdinaryCompactificationComparison
    (o : IntegralSystemRealization.Operations l E) (r : Realizations l E D o)
    (t : Compactification.Triangle f g)
    [QuasiCompact t.cf.i] [QuasiCompact t.cg.i] [QuasiCompact t.cfg.i] [QuasiCompact t.q]
    (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X) (lo hi torLo torHi : ℤ)
    (_hK : bridgeDomain l E D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) o t K lo hi torLo torHi) :
    semilinearComparison l E D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) o r t K =
      (ordinaryComparison l E D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl)
        r t).app K
